cavalieri_2026.title: Michigan Bridge Design Standards and Guides, MDOT Bridge Week, March 17-19 2026 (60-slide deck)
cavalieri_2026.use: Corroboration only: slide 8 shows Bridge Design Guide 8.43.01 (issued 02/24/25) sole-plate lengths 1'-4" Type I, 1'-6" Type II, 1'-10" Type III, 2'-2" Type IV and 70" I-beam, 2'-11 3/8" Michigan 1800, 3'-4" Bulb Tee. The 3'-4" bulb-tee value equals the 3'-4" bottom-flange width on BTB 002. No section is dimensioned in the deck.

source_status: research-report recommended design (MDOT OR15-182 App. K, sheets dated 05/09/18); not an MDOT standard

geometry_notes: All outline dimensions printed: overall depth x width, top and bottom slab thickness (dimension from face to void), web thickness ('5" (TYP)' or '4" (TYP)'), void corner chamfers ('1 1/2" (TYP)' both legs for 17/21 in; '3" (TYP)' both legs for 27-48 in) and '1/2" BEVEL (TYP)' at the two soffit corners.
Top corners are square (no bevel drawn). Void = width - 2*web by depth - top - bottom slab, centred.
Gross midspan section; end blocks (3'-0"), 2 in preformed holes, strands and reinforcement omitted.

shear_key_in.estimate_basis: The key's horizontal offsets are not dimensioned and the sheets are marked NO SCALE (the overall width is drawn about 1.6x too wide relative to the 5"/4" web callouts). Offsets were measured on 400 dpi renders against the local 3"/4"/5" callouts on the 17x36 and 27x48 interior sections: top setback 0.38-0.39 in, recess 0.78-0.81 in, upper transition ~45 deg, lower slope ~0.75 in rise x 0.8 in run. Rounded to 3/8 in setback, 3/4 in recess with 45 deg transitions (upper 3/8 x 3/8, lower 3/4 x 3/4). The 4" key height is taken from the start of the upper transition to the start of the lower slope, as drawn.

geometry_notes: Interior beams carry the shear key on both sides; fascia beams on the interior side only ('OMIT SHEAR KEY' on the exterior face). In this module the fascia key is on the -x side and the exterior face is +x, as drawn.
Nominal width (36 or 48 in) is the width below the key; the top 3 in zone is narrower by 2 x top_setback (interior) or 1 x top_setback (fascia) - estimate.
Fascia beams have a 9" top slab (void lowered) for the barrier anchorage; the 17x36 fascia section is drawn with no void (solid), and is implemented solid.
Web thickness is measured from the full-width face below the key: 5" (17x36), 4" (48 in wide).
Gross midspan section; end blocks, transverse post-tensioning ducts, strands and reinforcement omitted.

bulb_tee.sheet: BTB 002, PDF p43 (Sections A-A/B-B, both halves)

transcription.top_flange: 4'-1" wide; right chain 5" edge; left chain 5" + 3" + 3"; horizontal 1'-5 1/2" (edge to fillet start) + 3" fillet run; 11" total top zone
transcription.bottom_flange: 3'-4" wide; 3/4" BEVEL (TYP); chain 5 1/2" + 7" + 2" = 1'-2 1/2"; 1'-2" taper run + 2" fillet run

geometry_notes: Depth-parametric: only the web height changes (3'-0", 3'-6" or 4'-0").
Section B-B (midspan) and A-A (end) have the same concrete outline. The 3/4 in bevel is at the soffit corners only.
Distinct from WSDOT WF (6 1/8 in web, 38 3/8 in bottom flange), PCI BT and PCI NEBT (48 in top). Brice et al. (2021) appendix has no Michigan table.

published_weights.note: BEAM DIMENSIONS table 'APPROX WEIGHT (TONS)' by span (US short tons). The printed weights equal gross area x T x 150 pcf, where T = 70'-0"..110'-0" is the table's T row (Y is a longer forming length and does not fit). Independent area check.
